description: GEER Anchorage Alaska Earthquake is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Kevin Franke, Brigham Young University (byu.edu). GEER formed a reconnaissance team to investigate the effects of the the Anchorage, Alaska M7.0 30 November 2018 earthquake. Data in this project includes LiDAR and UAV photogrammetry point clouds (LAS and Potree files) along with photos from the team's field survey. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project. Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-2aqj-z033. Keywords: Earthquake reconnaissance, geotechnical earthquake engineering, Alaska, Anchorage, earthquake, M7.0. Published 2020-02-01. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
